## A flux from space {#diffuse-flux}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### IceCube, 2013

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/icecube/bert-ernie.png){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 300px;" fig-alt="IceCube event displays of Bert and Ernie: hundreds of optical modules lit by two cascades near 1 PeV."}

::: {.small}
**How to read σ and $p$:**

- $p$ is the probability of getting such an excess by chance if there are no cosmic neutrinos.
- σ says the same in “standard deviations”: the larger σ, the smaller $p$.
- $3\sigma$: $p\approx10^{-3}$, evidence; $5\sigma$: $p\approx3\cdot10^{-7}$, discovery.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="41%"}
::: {.takeaway}
Neutrinos from space exist.
:::

**IceCube, May 2010 – May 2012**

- 28 events with energies from 30 TeV to 1.2 PeV.
- About 10 were expected from the atmosphere.
- Among them Bert and Ernie: 1.04 ± 0.16 and 1.14 ± 0.17 PeV.
- A purely atmospheric origin is rejected at $4.1\sigma$.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube, Science (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5238v2) · event displays: IceCube Collaboration / IceCube–NSF, [IceCube (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5356) · plot in the appendix
:::

### Baikal confirms

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/optical-modules/baikal-gvd-om-deployment.jpeg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 460px;" fig-alt="A Baikal-GVD optical module being deployed from the ice."}
:::
::: {.column width="41%"}
::: {.takeaway}
Another detector, another hemisphere: the same flux.
:::

**Baikal-GVD, 2018–2024**

- 18 upward-going cascades with energies above 15 TeV.
- Expected from the atmosphere: $2.8\pm1.0$.
- Significance $5.1\sigma$.
- Water instead of ice.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[Baikal-GVD (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01893v2) · plot in the appendix
:::

::::::

### Baikal above 200 TeV

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="63%"}
![](media/films/gvd_cascades_sky_en.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 480px;" fig-alt="Eight Baikal-GVD cascades above 200 TeV on a sky map around the Galactic plane, a frame from the film."}
:::
::: {.column width="35%"}
::: {.takeaway}
The Galaxy may give more than expected.
:::

**8 cascades above 200 TeV**

- They crowd towards the Galactic plane.
- Baikal-GVD: $p=1.4\cdot10^{-2}$.
- Together with IceCube: $p=3.4\cdot10^{-4}$.
:::

## The first sources {#first-sources}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### NGC 1068

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/source-results/ngc1068-hubble-2025.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 500px;" fig-alt="The galaxy NGC 1068 imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope."}

::: {.media-caption}
ESA/Hubble & NASA, L. C. Ho, D. Thilker
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.takeaway}
Neutrinos escape where light cannot.
:::

**A Seyfert galaxy, about 47 million light years away**

- Its active nucleus is hidden behind dust.
- IceCube sees an excess of neutrinos from this direction: $4.0\sigma$ in 13 years.
- There are neutrinos, but almost no TeV gamma rays.
- Most likely the neutrinos are born in a dense region right next to the black hole, from which gamma rays cannot escape.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13403) · [IceCube, Science (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09972v1)
:::

### TXS 0506+056

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
<video class="slide-video" style="--media-max-height: 560px;" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" poster="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/source-results/icecube-170922a.jpg" src="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/source-results/icecube-170922a.mp4" aria-label="Recorded IceCube-170922A event."></video>
:::
::: {.column width="34%"}
::: {.takeaway}
A flaring blazar: the first candidate.
:::

**22 September 2017**

- A neutrino of about 290 TeV.
- A blazar flares in its direction: Fermi-LAT and MAGIC see it.
- A coincidence at about $3\sigma$.
- **2021:** a 224 TeV Baikal cascade from the same region of the sky. A candidate, not yet a proof.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube et al., Science (2018)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.08816) · [Baikal-GVD, ICRC 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13686v1)
:::

::::::

## The record: KM3-230213A {#record}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
<video class="slide-video" style="--media-max-height: 560px;" controls muted playsinline preload="metadata" poster="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/events/km3-230213a.jpg" src="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/events/km3-230213a.mp4" aria-label="Official KM3NeT event display of KM3-230213A."></video>
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
::: {.takeaway}
The most energetic neutrino ever.
:::

**13 February 2023, Mediterranean Sea**

- The KM3NeT/ARCA telescope.
- A muon of about 120 PeV crosses the detector almost horizontally.
- The neutrino energy is about 220 PeV.
- Where it came from is still unknown.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
KM3NeT Collaboration · [Nature (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08543-1)
:::
